Synagogue in Ansbach

Former Synagogue · Ansbach, Germany

The synagogue in Ansbach was built between 1744 and 1746 to designs by court architect Leopoldo Retti, its plain exterior deliberately concealing an ornate Baroque interior with an original Torah ark and bimah. During the November 1938 pogrom, the city's mayor ordered that the building not be set alight, though its interior fittings and religious texts were damaged. After the war it briefly served displaced Jewish persons and American soldiers before being renovated in the late 1940s. As Ansbach's Jewish community did not re-form, the synagogue was rededicated in 1964 as a symbolic and museum space, and today hosts cultural events and guided tours rather than religious services.
